commits.message:
feat(taxonomy): fix job-title extraction bug, dedupe near-duplicate candidates, add boilerplate-pattern learning + Job Titles page

Four pieces investigating a reported "job title saved in skills" bug
and the review queue's growing volume.

1. Verified the actual reported bug never existed: approved job titles
   were always landing correctly in job_titles.json, never mixed into
   canonical_skills.json (checked directly against both files). The
   real gap was visibility -- there was no page to browse approved job
   titles, only Skills taxonomy, so an approved title appeared to
   vanish. Added JobTitlesTaxonomyPage.tsx, mirroring the Skills page
   (search/filter/sort, no edit -- job titles have no description field
   to edit), wired into the nav next to Skills taxonomy.

2. Found a real, separate bug while investigating: a vendor format
   lists "Position: 1" (an ordinal) with the real title one line later
   under "Title:". "Position" being a Job Title label alias meant
   _extract_labeled_value found "Position: 1" first and returned the
   literal digit "1" as job_title -- queued as a taxonomy candidate 25+
   times over. Fixed with _is_plausible_job_title (app/email_parsing/
   parsers.py) -- a real title always has a letter -- which rejects the
   ordinal and falls through to an explicit "Title:" search instead.
   Defense in depth: find_unknown_job_title (app/understanding/taxonomy/
   candidates.py) now also rejects a purely-numeric value before it can
   ever reach the queue, regardless of which upstream parser produced it.

3. The same vendor's title also showed up as several separate
   candidates purely because a location/work-mode tag was baked onto
   the title text -- "AEM Solutions Engineer Lead- NY Onsite" vs "AEM
   Solutions Lead IN Brooklyn" are the same underlying role. find_unknown
   _job_title now strips these two specific, low-risk trailing shapes
   (a dash + onsite/remote/hybrid, "IN <City>", or a bare "(Remote)"/
   "(Onsite)"/"(Hybrid)") before dedup, collapsing variants into one
   candidate -- a genuinely distinguishing trailing parenthetical like
   "(Specialized Automation)" is never touched.

4. New boilerplate-pattern learning queue, same detect-then-approve
   shape as an unrecognized skill or job title: a line in a finished
   job_description that recurs verbatim across 3+ distinct sender
   domains (real content from unrelated companies is extremely unlikely
   to be byte-identical; a relay/template's injected line is) gets
   queued as signal_type='boilerplate_line'. Approving inserts it into
   the new approved_boilerplate_lines table and it's stripped from every
   future posting immediately, no redeploy -- the same live-immediately
   contract as approving a skill or job title. The 3-domain threshold is
   enforced in list_taxonomy_candidates itself, so a real posting's own
   (single-company) content never floods the review queue further.
   ModerationPage.tsx now shows two sections -- "Taxonomy candidates"
   (skill/job_title, with a Type column) and "Boilerplate patterns" --
   sharing the same bulk-select/approve/reject machinery per section.

New coverage: a Position:N ordinal is never read as a title, both at
the parser and at the candidate-queue layer; location/work-mode title
variants collapse into one candidate while a real distinguishing
parenthetical survives; a boilerplate line stays hidden below the
distinct-domain threshold and becomes visible once it crosses it; too-
short/too-long lines are never queued; approving a boilerplate line
strips it from a real posting immediately with no redeploy; boilerplate
candidates never leak into the skill/job_title queues. Full regression
suite (18 checks, 9 new) green against a fresh schema and rebuilt
image; frontend type-checks and builds clean.
